lalo: The powdered leaves of the baobab tree, used by the Africans to mix in their soup, as the southern negroes use powdered sassafras. Cf. Couscous.
labyrinthal: Pertaining to, or resembling, a labyrinth; intricate; labyrinthian.
laxness: The state of being lax; laxity.
langteraloo: An old game at cards. See Loo (a) Tatler.

laryngologist: One who applies himself to laryngology.

lacteously: In a lacteous manner; after the manner of milk.

lardon: A bit of fat pork or bacon used in larding.
latitat: A writ based upon the presumption that the person summoned was hiding. Blackstone.
lanseh: The small, whitish brown fruit of an East Indian tree (Lansium domesticum). It has a fleshy pulp, with an agreeable subacid taste. Balfour.
laudation: The act of lauding; praise; high commendation.
laureled: Crowned with laurel, or with a laurel wreath; laureate. [Written also laurelled.]
lapstreak: Made with boards whose edges lap one over another; clinker- built; -- said of boats.
lapling: One who has been fondled to excess; one fond of ease and sensual delights; -- a term of contempt.
labyrinthodonta: An extinct order of Amphibia, including the typical genus Labyrinthodon, and many other allied forms, from the Carboniferous, Permian, and Triassic formations. By recent writers they are divided into two or more orders. See Stegocephala.
lazarly: Full of sores; leprous. Shak. Bp. Hall.
lapislazuli: An albuminous mineral of a rich blue color. Same as Lazuli, which see.
lammergeier: A very large vulture (Gypaëtus barbatus), which inhabits the mountains of Southern Europe, Asia, and Northern Africa. When full- grown it is nine or ten feet in extent of wings. languid: 1. Drooping or flagging from exhaustion; indisposed to exertion; without animation; weak; weary; heavy; dull. " Languid, powerless limbs. " Armstrong. lathe: Formerly, a part or division of a county among the Anglo- Saxons. At present it consists of four or five hundreds, and is confined to the county of Kent. [Written also lath.] Brande & C. | 1. laminar: In, or consisting of, thin plates or layers; having the form of a thin plate or lamina.
lancet: 1. A surgical instrument of various forms, commonly sharp-pointed and two-edged, used in venesection, and in opening abscesses, etc. 2. (Metal.) languet: 1. Anything resembling the tongue in form or office; specif., the slip of metal in an organ pipe which turns the current of air toward its mouth. 2. That part of the hilt, in certain kinds of swords, which overlaps the scabbard.
lagnappe: In Louisiana, a trifling present given to customers by tradesmen; a gratuity. Lagniappe . . .is something thrown in, gratis, for good measure. Mark Twain.
laity: 1. The people, as distinguished from the clergy; the body of the people not in orders. A rising up of the laity against the sacerdotal caste. Macaulay. 2. The state of a layman. lactometer: An instrument for estimating the purity or richness of milk, as a measuring glass, a specific gravity bulb, or other apparatus.
laic: Of or pertaining to a layman or the laity. "Laical literature." Lowell. An unprincipled, unedified, and laic rabble. Milton.

latibulum: A concealed hiding place; a burrow; a lair; a hole.

laziness: The state or quality of being lazy. Laziness travels so slowly, that Poverty soon overtakes him. Franklin.

lacewing: Any one of several species of neuropterous insects of the genus Chrysopa and allied genera. They have delicate, lacelike wings and brilliant eyes. Their larvæ are useful in destroying aphids. Called also lace-winged fly, and goldeneyed fly.
lake: A pigment formed by combining some coloring matter, usually by precipitation, with a metallic oxide or earth, esp. with aluminium hydrate; as, madder lake; Florentine lake; yellow lake, etc. | A kind of fine white linen, formerly in use. (old) Chaucer.
lashing: The act of one who, or that which, lashes; castigation; chastisement. South. Lashing out, a striking out; also, extravagance.
laze: To be lazy or idle. [Colloq.] Middleton. | To waste in sloth; to spend, as time, in idleness; as, to laze away whole days. [Colloq.]
lambkill: A small American ericaceous shrub (Kalmia angustifolia); -- called also calfkill, sheepkill, sheep laurel, etc. It is supposed to poison sheep and other animals that eat it at times when the snow is deep and they cannot find other food.
lata: A convulsive tic or hysteric neurosis prevalent among Malays, similar to or identical with miryachit and jumping disease, the person affected performing various involuntary actions and making rapid inarticulate ejaculations in imitation of the actions and words of another person.
labored: Bearing marks of labor and effort; elaborately wrought; not easy or natural; as, labored poetry; a labored style.
lawsuit: An action at law; a suit in equity or admiralty; any legal proceeding before a court for the enforcement of a claim.
landslide: 1. The slipping down of a mass of land from a mountain, hill, etc. 2. The land which slips down.
layette: The outfit of clothing, blankets, etc., prepared for a newborn infant, and placed ready for used.
lachrymals: Tears; also, lachrymal feelings or organs. [Colloq.] People go to the theaters to have . . . their risibles and lachrymals set agoing. The Lutheran.
laborless: Not involving labor; not laborious; easy.
labially: In a labial manner; with, or by means of, the lips.
lathreeve: Formerly, the head officer of a lathe. See 1st Lathe.
lamination: The process of laminating, or the state of being laminated.
lavoesium: A supposed new metallic element. It is said to have been discovered in pyrites, and some other minerals, and to be of a silver-white color, and malleable.
laches: Neglect; negligence; remissness; neglect to do a thing at the proper time; delay to assert a claim. It ill became him to take advantage of such a laches with the eagerness of a shrewd attorney. Macaulay.
laudable: 1. Worthy of being lauded; praiseworthy; commendable; as, laudable motives; laudable actions; laudable ambition. 2. (Med.) Healthy; salubrious; normal; having a disposition to promote healing; not noxious; as, laudable juices of the body; laudable pus. Arbuthnot.
lampas: An inflammation and swelling of the soft parts of the roof of the mouth immediately behind the fore teeth in the horse; -- called also lampers.
laveer: To beat against the wind; to tack. (old) Dryden.

lambskin: 1. The skin of a lamb; especially, a skin dressed with the wool on, and used as a mat. Also used adjectively. 2. A kind of woolen.

laster: A workman whose business it is to shape boots or shoes, or place leather smoothly, on lasts; a tool for stretching leather on a last.
laminating: Forming, or separating into, scales or thin layers.
laticiferous: Containing the latex; -- applied to the tissue or tubular vessels in which the latex of the plant is found.
landlouper: A vagabond; a vagrant. [Written also landleaper and landloper.] "Bands of landloupers." Moltey.
lancely: Like a lance. Sir P. Sidney.
laurite: A rare sulphide of osmium and ruthenium found with platinum in Borneo and Oregon.
lagophthalmia: A morbid condition in which the eye stands wide open, giving a peculiar staring appearance.
landau: A four-wheeled covered vehicle, the top of which is divided into two sections which can be let down, or thrown back, in such a manner as to make an open carriage. [Written also landaw.]
lag: 1. Coming tardily after or behind; slow; tardy. (old) Came too lag to see him buried. Shak. 2. Last; long-delayed; -- obsolete, except in the phrase lag end. "The lag end of my life." lagopous: Having a dense covering of long hair, like the foot of a hare.
landtrost: (a) A chief magistrate in rural districts. He was replaced in 1827 by "resident magistrates." (b) The president of the Heemraad.
lallation: An imperfect enunciation of the letter r, in which it sounds like l.
langued: Tongued; having the tongue visible. Lions . . . represented as armed and langued gules. Cussans. LANGUE D'OC Langue` d'oc". lancination: A tearing; laceration. "Lancinations of the spirit." Jer. Taylor.
latah: A convulsive tic or hysteric neurosis prevalent among Malays, similar to or identical with miryachit and jumping disease, the person affected performing various involuntary actions and making rapid inarticulate ejaculations in imitation of the actions and words of another person.
laurin: A white crystalline substance extracted from the fruit of the bay (Laurus nobilis), and consisting of a complex mixture of glycerin ethers of several organic acids.
ladykin: A little lady; -- applied by the writers of Queen Elizabeth's time, in the abbreviated form Lakin, to the Virgin Mary. Note: The diminutive does not refer to size, but is equivalent to "dear." Brewer.

latency: The state or quality of being latent. To simplify the discussion, I shall distinguish three degrees of this latency. Sir W. Hamilton.
laid: of Lay. Laid paper, paper marked with parallel lines or water marks, as if ribbed, from parallel wires in the mold. It is called blue laid, cream laid, etc., according to its color.
lac: One hundred thousand; also, a vaguely great number; as, a lac of rupees. lawsonia: An Asiatic and North African shrub (Lawsonia inermis), with smooth oval leaves, and fragrant white flowers. Henna is prepared from the leaves and twigs. In England the shrub is called Egyptian privet, and in the West Indies, Jamaica mignonette.
lancefish: A slender marine fish of the genus Ammodytes, especially Ammodytes tobianus of the English coast; -- called also sand lance.
lactonic: Of, pertaining to, or derived from, lactone. | Pertaining to, or designating, an acid obtained by the oxidation of milk sugar (lactose).
laniary: Lacerating or tearing; as, the laniary canine teeth. | 1. The shambles; a place of slaughter. 2. (Anat.) A laniary, or canine, tooth.
larviform: Having the form or structure of a larva.
lamina: 1. A thin plate or scale; a laying over another; -- said of thin plates or platelike substances, as of bone or minerals. 2. (Bot.) lancewood: A tough, elastic wood, often used for the shafts of gigs, archery bows, fishing rods, and the like. largo: Slow or slowly; -- more so than adagio; next in slowness to grave, which is also weighty and solemn. -- n. A movement or piece in largo time.

lachrymatory: A "tear-bottle;" a narrow-necked vessel found in sepulchers of the ancient Romans; -- so called from a former notion that the tears of the deceased person's friends were collected in it. Called also lachrymal or lacrymal.
lachrymal: 1. Of or pertaining to tears; as, lachrymal effusions. 2. (Anat.) (a) Pertaining to, or secreting, tears; as, the lachrymal gland. (b) Pertaining to the lachrymal organs; as, lachrymal bone; lachrymal duct.
lafayette: (a) The dollar fish. (b) A market fish, the goody, or spot (Liostomus xanthurus), of the southern coast of the United States.
laconian: Of or pertaining to Laconia, a division of ancient Greece; Spartan. -- n. An inhabitant of Laconia; esp., a Spartan.
ladino: One of the half-breed descendants of whites and Indians; a mestizo; -- so called throughout Central America. They are usually of a yellowish orange tinge. Am. Cyc.

lardoon: A bit of fat pork or bacon used in larding.

laryngophony: The sound of the voice as heard through a stethoscope when the latter is placed upon the larynx.
labioplasty: A plastic operation for making a new lip, or for replacing a lost tissue of a lip.

lacklustre: A want of luster. -- a. Wanting luster or brightness. "Lackluster eye." Shak.
landlocked: 1. Inclosed, or nearly inclosed, by land. 2. (Zoöl.) Confined to a fresh-water lake by reason of waterfalls or dams; -- said of fishes that would naturally seek the sea, after spawning; as, the landlocked salmon.
laboratory: The workroom of a chemist; also, a place devoted to experiments in any branch of natural science; as, a chemical, physical, or biological laboratory. Hence, by extension, a place where something is prepared, or some operation is performed; as, the liver is the laboratory of the bile.

latirostrous: Having a broad beak. Sir T. Browne.

lathereeve: Formerly, the head officer of a lathe. See 1st Lathe.
lactage: The produce of animals yielding milk; milk and that which is made from it.

lampooner: The writer of a lampoon. "Libelers, lampooners, and pamphleteers." Tatler.
lacwork: Ornamentation by means of lacquer painted or carved, or simply colored, sprinkled with gold or the like; -- said especially of Oriental work of this kind.
laqueary: Using a noose, as a gladiator. [Obs. or R.] Retiary and laqueary combatants. Sir T. Browne.
lamellarly: Flat and thin; lamelliform; composed of lamellæ. -- Lam"el*lar*ly, adv. In thin plates or scales.
larghetto: Somewhat slow or slowly, but not so slowly as largo, and rather more so than andante.
labellum: 1. (Bot.) The lower or apparently anterior petal of an orchidaceous flower, often of a very curious shape. 2. (Zoöl.) A small appendage beneath the upper lip or labrum of certain insects.
